name: Estimation Station
description: How many jelly beans fill the jar? Everyone guesses a number, the closest guesses earn the most, and the class average is the one to beat. Swap in your own how-many challenges.
when: When a number is worth arguing about, and you want every guess on the board before the answer.
recommendedFor: Use to open a math or science lesson with a number nobody knows offhand. Write three challenges with real answers; the console can also set the answer during a round.

questions.prompt: How many jelly beans would fill a 1-gallon jar?
How many times does an average person's heart beat in a single day?
How many grains of rice are in a single cup?

intro.message:
ESTIMATION STATION!

Each round you'll see a 'how many...?' challenge. Type your best estimate, no need to be exact, just reason it out.

Closest guesses earn the most points. And watch the class's average guess: a whole room together is usually closer than almost anyone alone.

q1.prompt:
Estimate 1 of 3:

How many jelly beans would fill a 1-gallon jar?

q2.prompt:
Estimate 2 of 3:

How many times does an average person's heart beat in a single day?

q3.prompt:
Estimate 3 of 3:

How many grains of rice are in a single cup?

end.message: Nice estimating, everyone! The more you practice, the sharper your number sense gets.
